projects.name: Access to quality health services for refugees and vulnerable host populations is reinforced through strengthened national health systems and coordinated multi-sectoral interventions, ensuring continuity of care.
projects.description:
UNHCR will continue working with the Ministry of Health, WHO, UNAIDS, UNFPA, and health partners to ensure that refugees and vulnerable Moldovan populations (including Roma communities, persons with disabilities and older persons) have equitable access to essential health services. In 2025, UNHCR will support access to primary healthcare, emergency and trauma care, sexual and reproductive health (including clinical management of rape), immunization, perinatal care, mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS), and services related to gender-based violence (GBV). Support will also focus on HIV and STI prevention and harm reduction through community outreach activities, including peer support and information dissemination, particularly targeting hard-to-reach populations and groups at increased risk, such as LGBTIQ+ individuals, persons living with HIV, sex workers, and Roma refugees​. UNHCR, UNAIDS and local partners will continue supporting access to HIV-related services for key affected populations within the refugee community along with case management and psychosocial support. Also through local partners and in coordination with local public authorities, UNHCR will provide gynecological consultations for refugees.

To strengthen access to care, UNHCR, in close coordination with WHO, UNFPA and IOM, will continue supporting the inclusion of refugees in national health systems, including access to public health insurance through advocacy and technical support. UNHCR will also contribute to improved access to essential medicines, specialist consultations, rehabilitative and palliative care, and ensure that referral pathways to public services are functional and accessible. Outreach interventions, including mobile health teams and information sessions, will be reach underserved regions and populations with mobility challenges or barriers to health access, such as older persons and persons with disabilities​.

projects.name: Social cohesion and refugee inclusion are enhanced through Participatory Community Projects (PCPs), Community Support Initiatives (CSIs), and the Cities of Solidarity initiative, fostering mutual understanding and resilience among refugees and host communities.
projects.description:
UNHCR will continue to promote social cohesion and community resilience by implementing Participatory Community Projects (PCPs) and Community Support Initiatives (CSIs) that foster engagement between refugees and host communities. These initiatives will include joint community-led projects, improvement of shared infrastructure, and rehabilitation of locally managed public spaces, ensuring that both communities collaborate to address shared needs. Projects will prioritize inclusive design and participation, with specific outreach to persons with disabilities, Roma community members, older persons, youth, women, boys and girls, in line with UNHCR’s commitment to age, gender, and diversity (AGD) inclusive programming​. UNHCR will continue to support Community Service Centers in key locations hosting refugees. 

Under the Cities of Solidarity initiative, UNHCR will continue working with municipalities to develop and implement local action plans that enhance refugee inclusion in social protection, employment, and local development programmes. These plans will be developed through participatory assessments and dialogue between local authorities, civil society, refugees, and vulnerable host community members, and will promote long-term urban resilience. UNHCR will provide technical assistance, financial support, and policy guidance to ensure that local action plans are inclusive of marginalized groups, including Roma and persons with disabilities, and reflect their specific needs and contributions​.

To further strengthen refugee participation in local decision-making, UNHCR will support the establishment of Refugee Committees in key locations and promote their formal inclusion in municipal structures and coordination mechanisms. These bodies will represent the diverse refugee population, including older persons, Roma, persons with disabilities, LGBTIQ+ individuals, and youth, ensuring their voices are reflected in local governance. UNHCR will also invest in capacity-building for refugee leaders, enabling them to engage in advocacy and community planning in a meaningful and sustained manner. These efforts will help build inclusive, cohesive, and accountable communities, in line with Moldova’s commitment to refugee protection and social inclusion.

projects.name: Access to private housing for refugees is expanded through rental subsidies, small-scale housing rehabilitation combined with tenure security guarantees, and inclusion in Moldova’s national affordable housing schemes, supporting long-term, sustainable living arrangements.
projects.description:
Access to stable, adequate housing is a catalyst for all other aspects of refugees’ self-reliance—enabling people to settle, seek employment, enrol their children in school, and fully participate in community life.

UNHCR will promote access to private housing solutions through rental assistance programs, small-scale repairs, and advocacy for refugee inclusion in Moldova’s affordable housing schemes. These efforts will primarily target economically active refugees who are able to progressively assume responsibility for their housing costs, ensuring that rental assistance remains a transitional and sustainable form of support.

Rental subsidies will act as a stabilizing measure—helping refugees move out of temporary arrangements, focus on livelihoods, and build the foundations for independent living. Small-scale rehabilitation will target property owners hosting refugees, with improvements offered in exchange for hosting arrangements that include tenure security guarantees. This supports more vulnerable refugees, reinforces community-based coping mechanisms, and offers a pathway toward affordable, longer-term housing.

In parallel, UNHCR will advocate for refugees’ inclusion in national affordable housing schemes, including favourable loan conditions and first-time homeownership programs.

projects.name: Access to employment, entrepreneurship, and financial services for refugees and stateless persons is improved through strengthened public-private partnerships, targeted skills development, and inclusive labor market support.
projects.description:
UNHCR will promote the economic inclusion of refugees and stateless persons by supporting access to formal employment, entrepreneurship, and financial services. In coordination with the National Employment Agency (NEA), the Ministry of Labour and Social Protection (MLSP), and development actors, UNHCR will facilitate job placement, Romanian language classes, vocational training, and job counselling, with an emphasis on overcoming specific barriers faced by women, older persons, and persons with disabilities. Efforts will include expanding access to childcare options to better support the participation of female-headed households in the labor market.

To address broader structural barriers, UNHCR will support the recognition of qualifications, raise awareness among employers on refugee rights to work, and promote inclusive labor market policies. Collaboration with private sector stakeholders and financial institutions (such as the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development) will support entrepreneurship training and access to business development services, particularly for refugees with limited financial resources or who face intersectional discrimination, including Roma refugees and persons with disabilities​.

Economic inclusion initiatives will be embedded in broader inclusion strategies, including the Cities of Solidarity initiative, and implemented in partnership with local authorities. UNHCR will promote gathering evidence on the socio-economic indicators and area-based approaches that extend support to both refugees and host communities. These efforts will prioritize equity, ensuring that refugees of all ages, genders, and backgrounds are empowered to achieve self-reliance and contribute to Moldova’s socio-economic development​.

projects.name: Inclusion of refugees in national social protection and housing systems is supported through the maintenance, transformation, and phased decommissioning of collective accommodation, with pathways to specialized and community-based housing solutions for individuals with heightened vulnerabilities.
projects.description:
UNHCR will continue to work closely with the MLSP and local public authorities to maintain a limited number of RACs, ensuring that they provide safe, dignified, and protection-sensitive conditions for individuals with heightened vulnerabilities. These include older persons, persons with disabilities, Roma refugees, and others who are unable to live independently due to physical, psychosocial, or social support needs.

Support will be provided for the ongoing maintenance and rehabilitation of these RACs, including essential repairs, accessibility improvements, and the provision of equipment to meet minimum living standards. UNHCR will also strengthen site management and coordination, with an emphasis on inclusive practices, accountability, and capacity-building of RAC staff. This will include training on protection-sensitive service delivery, inclusive communication, and referral mechanisms for specialized support.

As part of the broader RAC transition and decommissioning strategy, UNHCR will support the progressive consolidation of temporary RACs and facilitate the transition of residents to more sustainable, long-term solutions. In coordination with the MLSP and development partners, UNHCR will advocate for and support the inclusion of vulnerable refugees in Moldova’s existing institutional care systems, residential services, and social housing stock, in line with the government’s deinstitutionalization and community integration policies. UNHCR will also collaborate with MLSP to strengthen case management and referral systems for highly vulnerable individuals, ensuring that their needs are adequately assessed and that transitions out of RACs are voluntary, informed, and protection-sensitive. Special attention will be given to Roma communities and others at risk of exclusion from mainstream services.

To promote long-term solutions, UNHCR will engage in strategic advocacy and resource mobilization to expand Moldova’s inclusive housing and care infrastructure. This includes promoting investments in specialized and community-based accommodation, with a focus on persons with disabilities, older persons, and Roma refugees.

projects.name: Ensuring refugee women and girls have access to GBV prevention and response services through mobile and static WGSS (Women and Girls Safe Spaces)
projects.description:
UNFPA's Women and Girls  Safe Spaces are crucial in supporting the Moldovan government's efforts to ensure that refugees have effective access to protection. By providing GBV response services and prevention interventions, UNFPA helps to protect vulnerable groups and create a safe environment where refugees are offered support to address protection concerns. The 11 UNFPA's Mobile Safe Spaces are operating across all rayons in Moldova, addressing the challenge of uneven access to protection services for refugees across different regions. By expanding the reach of these safe spaces through mobile units, UNFPA aims to close gaps in geographic coverage of protection services, particularly in rural or remote areas. This ensure that refugees, regardless of their location, have access to essential support and resources. The 20 Static Safe Spaces are located in strategic locations, including Border Crossing Points, Transit Points, and in RACs hosting the most vulnerable refugees, including Roma and persons with disabilities. 

To contribute to strengthened social cohesion and peaceful coexistence between refugee and host communities, UNFPA's Safe Spaces foster dialogue through recreational and non-formal education activities involving both refugees and host community members. This is particularly important for youth and adolescents, who can benefit from shared experiences and opportunities for interaction. By creating a welcoming and inclusive environment, Safe Spaces help to build bridges between different communities and promote understanding and tolerance.

To address the emotional distress that refugees in Moldova experience, the Safe Spaces offer a critical space where refugees and host community members can access individual and group psychosocial support. This support is essential for improving mental health and psychosocial well-being, helping individuals to cope with the challenges of displacement and rebuild their lives.

Considering the importance of coordination at the local level on protection-related developments and measurements, the Safe Spaces coordinate closely with Local Public Authorities to ensure a comprehensive and effective response to the needs of refugees in Moldova.

UNFPA will implement in 2024-2025 the integration of GBV prevention and response in medico-social centers located in Vulcanesti and Ocnita. The program aims to enhance the capacity of home care employees to address GBV among individuals with disabilities and older adults with limited mobility. Key activities include finalizing SOPs on GBV integration, continuing staff training, and continue establishing a safe reporting space for women with limited mobility.

UNHCR will continue to strengthen gender-based violence (GBV) prevention, response, and risk mitigation efforts by ensuring that refugees and other vulnerable populations, including Roma women, LGBTIQ+ persons, sex workers and persons with disabilities, have access to specialized and survivor-centered GBV services. This includes safe shelter, GBV case management, legal assistance, and mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS), delivered in coordination with government authorities, UN agencies, and civil society actors​. UNHCR will continue supporting the MLSP through technical capacity aiming at meeting the standards of the Istanbul Convention for service provision.

Mobile and community-based teams will enhance outreach, particularly to underserved areas and groups facing compounded barriers, such as Roma women and sex workers. UNHCR’s Roma-led partner will work to connect Roma GBV survivors to available services, recognizing the systemic discrimination and structural obstacles they may face. Legal services for GBV cases will be provided.

UNHCR will replicate good practices such as support to women-led organizations (WLOs) and the localization of the Girl Shine curriculum, which will be implemented with adolescent girls and their caregivers. The office will work on tailored communication materials on GBV and gender equality for Roma women, based on a 2024 study conducted with a WLO. Additionally, group psychosocial support and skills development workshops will continue, integrating content on mental health, sexual and reproductive health, and online safety, and creating safe spaces for survivors to seek help. UNHCR's Roma-led partner will carry out group activities with Roma women to provide them with life skills and information, empowering them to make decisions about their own lives.

projects.description:
UNFPA is committed to enhancing the quality and accessibility of specialized services for survivors of gender-based violence (GBV) by working closely with the Government to revitalize two GBV shelters. This initiative focuses on creating inclusive environments that cater to the diverse needs of survivors, particularly those with disabilities.
Key Components of the Initiative:
1. Infrastructure and Accessibility Improvements: Upgrading the physical infrastructure of the shelters to ensure compliance with accessibility standards. Adding features such as ramps, accessible bathrooms, and adaptive equipment to accommodate survivors with mobility, visual, or hearing impairments. In 2024-2025 UNFPA planned to revitalize one shelter in Rîscani, and one shelter in Stefan Vodă.
2. Capacity Building for Shelter Staff: Training shelter staff on inclusive practices to better support survivors with disabilities. Enhancing skills in providing trauma-informed and survivor-centered care.
Tailored Services for Survivors with Disabilities: Developing specialized support services, including psychosocial counseling, legal aid, and health care tailored to the needs of persons with disabilities.
Ensuring the inclusion of sign language interpreters, assistive devices, and other adaptive tools. Enhanced capacities of shelter psychologists to provide specialised care to GBV survivors. 
3. Comprehensive Mentoring and Supervision for Newly Established Shelters in Rîșcani and Ștefan Vodă: Implement a robust and tailored mentoring and supervision program for the newly established shelters in Rîșcani and Ștefan Vodă, aimed at enhancing operational efficiency and ensuring best practices in survivor care. This initiative will include regular on-site visits by experienced professionals, ongoing staff training, and the development of standardized protocols for shelter management. Additionally, there will be a focus on monitoring the shelters' ability to provide a safe, supportive, and empowering environment for survivors, with a particular emphasis on trauma-informed care and sustainable case management.

4. Equipping the Rîșcani Shelter and Family Justice Center with specialized, accessible vehicles designed to support the mobility needs of survivors with disabilities. This initiative will enhance the ability of these centers to provide safe transportation for individuals with physical and mobility challenges, ensuring that they have reliable access to essential services, including medical appointments, legal proceedings, and other support activities. Furthermore, the initiative will involve training staff on how to properly assist survivors during transportation, emphasizing dignity and independence.

2. Equipping Two Shelters (CAP and ProFamilia) with Vehicles for Outreach and Community Engagement Activities: Procure and equip two strategically located shelters—CAP and ProFamilia—with specialized vehicles to support comprehensive outreach programs in surrounding communities. These vehicles will facilitate mobile services such as awareness campaigns, educational workshops, and direct support for survivors who may not have access to shelter services. The outreach vehicles will also enable quick deployment for emergency interventions and provide an essential resource for engaging with vulnerable populations in remote or underserved areas. This strategic initiative will not only increase the shelters' visibility but will also expand their ability to deliver critical services to those in need.

projects.name: (UNFPA) Supporting the National Agency on EVAW and domestic violence to develop and strengthen GBV Data Collection Mechanism, multi sectoral GBV response and national campaigns against GBV
projects.description:
UNFPA is supporting Agency on EVAW and DV to develop data collection and analysis for improved protection services. The initiative aims to improve data accuracy, streamline processes, ultimately leading to better service delivery for refugees and host community members. By supporting the national structures, UNFPA is also advancing the localization of the response, ensuring that quality GBV services are delivered by local actors. Additionally, UNFPA is facilitating a series of comprehensive capacity-building activities aimed at strengthening the skills and knowledge of multi-sectoral response teams, including social workers, healthcare providers, law enforcement, and other key stakeholders. These efforts focus on enhancing their ability to provide coordinated, survivor-centered services and effectively address the diverse needs of GBV survivors. Alongside these activities, UNFPA is also supporting the development and implementation of a nationwide campaign to raise awareness about gender-based violence, challenge harmful social norms, and promote community engagement in preventing violence and supporting survivors.

In addition, UNFPA worked to formulate a strategic vision for GBV services in Moldova:  A strategic framework for the UN Essential Services Package for Women and Girls Subject to Violence was developed and tailored to the Moldovan context to ensure the delivery of high-quality GBV services. This effort was complemented by a comprehensive gap analysis of GBV services across Moldova's rayons, evaluating both public and private service providers to identify deficiencies relative to the essential service package.

Building on the findings of the gap analysis, a Roadmap for Enhancing GBV Services was designed, including a three-year social investment plan to address identified challenges and foster the development of GBV services. Additionally, a pilot assessment of the performance and coordination of multi-disciplinary GBV teams was conducted in selected rayons to identify best practices and areas for improvement.

To further support these efforts, UNFPA provided targeted technical and material support to government institutions engaged in GBV prevention and response, strengthening their capacity and effectiveness in addressing GBV challenges. Through these initiatives, UNFPA advanced the strategic vision and operational capabilities for GBV services in Moldova.

The schools were provided with necessary policies and instructions on establishing pupils’ councils and managing pupils’ engagement and participation in decision making processes.

UNICEF engaged and ensured that adolescents are empowered to claim for and shape youth friendly services and programs and have access to decision making processes. 2500 young volunteers’ members of pupils’ councils and centers were capacitated on peer-to-peer education, social innovation and civic engagement. This was possible as UNICEF organized two editions of the social innovation program UPSHIFT. During USPHIFT activities, 1400 adolescents benefited from a full cycle training on local mobilization, business development, startup management and implementation.  Working directly with 9 youth centers, UNICEF engaged 1,000 young volunteers in capacity building, outreach and peer to peer to 35,000 Moldovan and refugee adolescents and youth.

projects.name: Making all spaces safe for women and girls by preventing and responding to Technology-Facilitated GBV
projects.description:
National Laws Revision: Law No. 45/2007 was revised to include new definitions for "violence against women," "femicide," and "psychological violence," addressing violence facilitated through information technology. UNFPA and the Women’s Law Center analyzed the legal framework and developed a Compatibility Report on national laws and the Istanbul Convention, leading to amendments on TFGBV.

#BodyRight Campaign Advocacy: In November 2024, UNFPA Moldova launched the #BodyRight campaign with partners, focusing on digital violence and promoting positive online behavior. The campaign reached over 2 million people online and engaged 500 youth through policy dialogues, social media mobilization, and school outreach. It strengthened UNFPA’s position in TFGBV advocacy.

TFGBV Education and Prevention: UNFPA and La Strada developed a guideline on digital violence for social professionals, offering practical scenarios on online intimacy, sexting, harassment, and more. Over 40 professionals participated in a ToT, leading to awareness-raising activities reaching 400+ participants, including refugees and vulnerable groups.

Orange Foundation Partnership: The SuperCoders program, in collaboration with UNFPA’s #BodyRight campaign, introduced digital safety alongside coding education for youth. In 2024, the partnership expanded to train teachers in generative AI and promote digital safety awareness among adolescents and parents, fostering a safe, inclusive digital environment.

As the next step UNFPA is in the process of:
i) advocacy with telecom companies
ii) terminology on TFGBV development
iii) advocacy on legal amendments
iv) qualitative research on TFGBV
v) integrate TFGBV into GBV case management SOPs
vi) training of mass media on TFGBV, include development of a guide
vii) campaign on TFGBV
viii) integration of TFGBV into EduLife formal and informal curriculum
ix) social media scanning on harmful content
x) events with IT companies on safety by design guidelines

projects.name: (UNFPA) Provision of cash assistance into GBV Case Management for survivors from refugee and host communities
projects.description:
As part of the Ukrainian Refugee Response in Moldova and to address GBV related risks, UNFPA has integrated cash assistance within GBV case management, targeting GBV survivors and individuals at risk of GBV – including Ukrainian refugees and vulnerable Moldovans. 
Strengthening the empowerment of women and girls via high quality CM&Cash support is the main reason the initiative is being undertaken. The programme has been informed by a thorough gender/GBV analysis  the analysis has influenced the
design of the programme.
The cash component of the GBV case management aims to empower survivors, mitigate GBV risks, and to support survivors in accessing GBV services by addressing the economic barriers that hinder survivors from escaping abusive situations and accessing life-saving GBV services. The cash element is integrated within the GBV CM in conjunction with other service components, such as psychosocial support, referral to other services, self-esteem strengthening, capacity building for economic independence and women’s rights. Prior to initiating the integration of cash assistance in GBV case management, a response analysis was conducted to determine situations when cash would be considered a useful and appropriate intervention based on context-specific analysis of GBV situations in Moldova. The response analysis resulted in a Response Framework outlining the precise contexts and situations in which cash is an appropriate assistance modality capable of responding to the GBV needs and risks of women and girls. The framework aims to support caseworkers in the assessment and selection process for cash assistance. Cash transfers to bank accounts have been deemed the most appropriate cash delivery mechanism. The cash transfer value is calculated based on the vulnerability and need of each individual as per the case plan. A monitoring framework has been established to ensure a regular and systematic process of data collection and analysis of the integration of Cash in GBV case management. The purpose of the monitoring is to collect feedback that can improve the implementation of cash assistance in the case management process, and track its risks and benefits, in order to create better protection outcomes for survivors and individuals at risk of GBV. The monitoring framework includes different tools. Post Distribution Monitoring (PDM) surveys will be administered by the case worker to gather information from the survivors using a questionnaire. This information will be triangulated with data gathered from the Complaint and Feedback Mechanism (CFM). Output monitoring has been conducted to monitor the programme outreach, including the number of individuals reached with cash assistance interventions and the total value transferred directly to individuals for cash assistance. The monitoring includes disaggregated information on gender, age, disability, displacement status, number of dependents of survivors, number of installments, and delivery mechanism to enable regular trend analysis of the cash distribution. 
Process monitoring is conducted through the PDM surveys and monitoring of CFM, aimed to monitor the cash assistance distribution process to be able to capture any factors that may affect the quality, safety, and access of survivors to the cash assistance. The PDM surveys aim to capture whether the survivors deem the duration, timing, and amount of the cash assistance to be adequate to improve their safety, and whether the survivors were able to access cash assistance safely.

projects.name: Child protection mechanisms are strengthened to ensure the identification, referral, and support of refugee children at risk, including survivors of violence, gender-based violence (GBV), and unaccompanied and separated children (UASC).
projects.description:
UNHCR will work closely with the Ministry of Labor and Social Protection (MLSP), UNICEF, and key partners to enhance the capacity of Moldova’s national child protection system, ensuring that refugee and vulnerable Moldovan children have continuous and equitable access to essential services. This will involve capacity-building initiatives for child protection professionals, social workers, and local authorities to improve case management, referral mechanisms, and inter-agency coordination. Special attention will be given to the integration of refugee children and unaccompanied and separated children (UASC) into national child protection programs, ensuring they receive the same standard of care and protection as Moldovan children. Throughout this work, gender and disability mainstreaming will be systematically applied to ensure that girls and boys, including those with disabilities, are equally protected and supported.

UNHCR will support community-based child-friendly spaces, providing psychosocial support, safe spaces, and tailored services for children at risk of violence, neglect, exploitation, or family separation.Through protection desks, UNHCR and partners will support the identification of children at risk and ensure their referral to the national child protection system and access to child protection services, including systematic Best Interests Assessments (BIAs) for UASC. Additionally, UNHCR will assist in harmonizing legal and procedural frameworks to ensure that refugee children continue to be systematically included in Moldova’s national child protection policies and legal structures. Training for frontline service providers will emphasize inclusive and gender-sensitive approaches, focusing on mandatory reporting procedures, child protection case management, and the specific needs of children with disabilities, Roma children, survivors of abuse, and those at risk violence, neglect and/or abuse.

To guarantee long-term sustainability and equitable access to services, UNHCR will support the decentralization of protection services, ensuring that refugee and Moldovan children can receive support in urban and rural areas alike. Efforts will also focus on strengthening disaggregated data collection and monitoring systems, enabling authorities to track service delivery, identify protection gaps across population groups, and improve timely and inclusive responses. Through these interventions, UNHCR aims to contribute to a resilient, inclusive, and rights-based child protection system that meets the needs of all children.

projects.name: Out-of-school comprehensive sexuality education for youth, including young people with disabilities, is operationalized following international standards.
projects.description:
To complement the formal/school-based comprehensive sexuality education and reach out to adolescents and youth from vulnerable groups and remote areas, UNFPA has been supporting for many years the out-of-school programs. 
In 2023 UNFPA will continue implementing the out-of-school comprehensive sexuality education (CSE) program. This initiative will follow UNFPA’s International Technical and Programmatic Guidance on Out-of-School CSE and will focus on reaching adolescents and young people in rural areas, those with disabilities, and youth from the left bank of the Nistru River.
In 2024, the initiative aims to foster a more inclusive and supportive environment where all young people, regardless of their background, have access to comprehensive sexuality education and essential resources for a healthy and informed future. To achieve this, several institutions and organizations working with youth will be equipped with dedicated spaces for non-formal sexuality education activities.
Additionally, civil society organizations, particularly those in underserved regions, will receive support to enhance their capacity in promoting young people’s sexual and reproductive health and rights. Specialists from various organizations will be trained to deliver accurate, age-appropriate education on these topics, ensuring that young people are well-informed and empowered.
Furthermore, parents and caregivers of adolescents with disabilities will be provided with the necessary knowledge and resources to support their children’s development and smooth transition into adulthood.
In 2025, UNFPA will continue strengthening civil society organizations and youth networks across Moldova, including those on the left bank of the Nistru River, to develop and implement programs on sexual and reproductive health and rights tailored to diverse youth groups. To support these efforts, UNFPA will create guidelines for delivering youth-friendly health services for vulnerable youth, aligned with international out-of-school comprehensive sexuality education (OOS CSE) standards.
A digital training program will be introduced for facilitators working in CSE, ensuring they are well-equipped to provide accurate and effective education. Additionally, new educational and interactive materials, such as the Diary of an Adolescent Boy/Girl, will be developed to make information on sexual and reproductive health and rights more accessible and relevant to young people. 
Building on UNFPA Moldova’s expertise in youth well-being and global best practices, and in partnership with the Ministry of Education and Research (MER) and the Youth National Agency, UNFPA will establish the Future-Ready Hub—a pioneering space dedicated to life skills development, innovation, and modern technologies. Bringing together adolescents, youth educators, youth workers, NGOs, and the private sector, the Hub will foster a collaborative, forward-looking environment. 

In 2026, UNFPA will continue supporting NGOs to deliver out-of-school comprehensive sexuality education (CSE) programmes for adolescents and young people. Organizations trained in previous years will receive further support to reach adolescents with disabilities and those from rural areas or families affected by poverty, violence, and other vulnerabilities. NGOs will also be supported to integrate the Adolescent Diary into their programmes, both as a complementary resource and as a stand-alone CSE tool.
Healthcare providers from the left bank of the Nistru River will receive continuous supervision on specific health and CSE topics to strengthen their capacity to provide accurate, evidence-based, and youth-friendly medical and psychological services. In addition, they will be empowered and supported to act as trainers for local school staff.
As part of the operationalisation of the EduLIFE Hub, planned for launch this year, a regionally co-created curriculum and handbook on life skills will be developed. These resources will support educators in strengthening adolescents’ competencies in sexuality education and in developing the skills necessary to navigate modern societies.
Additionally, UNFPA will conduct a national youth-centered campaign to promote healthy and safe adolescent development, including targeted messages on the prevention of teenage pregnancy.

projects.name: Refugee and vulnerable Moldovan children, including Roma children and children with disabilities, have improved access to inclusive and quality formal education through targeted support, strengthened coordination, and capacity-building initiatives.
projects.description:
UNHCR will continue collaborating with the Ministry of Education and Research (MER) and UNICEF to ensure that refugee and vulnerable Moldovan children, adolescents, and youth have access to inclusive and quality formal education. Key efforts will focus on increasing enrollment rates in Moldovan schools, expanding access to preschool education, and ensuring that all refugee families are informed about school enrollment procedures. UNHCR will also support the endorsement and fundraising efforts for the costed roadmap on educational inclusion, ensuring that financial and technical assistance is available to sustain refugee education efforts.

To facilitate effective learning and integration, UNHCR will support targeted Romanian language classes, literacy programs, and catch-up education, particularly for Roma children and other marginalized groups facing barriers to school enrollment and retention. Schools will receive technical support and additional resources, and teacher training programs will be expanded to improve inclusive education methodologies. Furthermore, UNHCR will promote in-person education, mitigating risks associated with prolonged online learning and ensuring that refugee children can fully participate in classroom environments​.

Strengthening child protection and psychosocial support within the education system will remain a priority. UNHCR will work to enhance school-based protection mechanisms, ensuring that refugee and vulnerable Moldovan children have access to safe learning environments free from bullying and discrimination. In line with the new Temporary Protection Directive, and in coordination with UNICEF, UNHCR will support the MER to develop and implement the monitoring system to track refugee children access to education, including its modalities. Additionally, UNHCR will continue advocating for higher education opportunities for refugees, including exploring the potential rollout of the DAFI scholarship program in Moldova. Through these interventions, UNHCR aims to foster sustainable inclusion, ensuring that education serves as a pathway to protection, resilience, and future self-reliance for all refugee children, particularly those from marginalized backgrounds.

projects.name: (UNFPA) Strengthened capacity of the General Education system to deliver quality health education and create an enabling environment for students’ wellbeing and healthy development.
projects.description:
As part of its ongoing commitment to the Ministry of Education and Research (MER), UNFPA continues to enhance national capacity and policy in the education sector, empowering pupils and youth through life-skills development and supporting their safe transition to adulthood. UNFPA will provide sustained technical expertise to advance national priorities related to adolescent and youth well-being, comprehensive sexuality education (CSE), and safe and healthy development. Additionally, it will support MER in strengthening communication and promoting the roles of schools and families in education. 
In 2023, is formalising its collaboration with the Ministry of Education and Research by signing a Memorandum of Understanding for the 2023-2027 period. 
Following the International Technical Guidance on Sexuality Education and addressing national needs, UNFPA will support the Ministry in developing a health education school club for grades V-VII. In 2023, the curriculum and didactic resources will be developed, with pilot implementation and finalization planned for 2024. 
Additionally, UNFPA will piloted the EduLIFE School Program: friendly environment, access to health education, and menstrual hygiene products. This concept embodies a multidimensional approach to strengthening the educational institutions’ ability to contribute to students' well-being and life skills, encouraging healthy and non-violent behaviour, promoting equal learning opportunities for both girls and boy
In 2024, UNFPA is expanding the "EduLIFE School" model to four new schools, including two designated as Model Schools. This initiative will promote a student-friendly environment, comprehensive sexuality education, and access to menstrual hygiene products. The selection of schools will be carried out in collaboration with the Ministry of Education, with two institutions being reorganized to accommodate refugee students from Ukraine. Key implementing partners will include the NGO “Youth Media Center” and the platform “suntparinte.md.”
In 2025, alongside with other UN agencies, UNFPA is assisting MER in conducting a national school survey among pupils, parents, and teachers. The survey will assess education quality, student participation, informal payments, rights awareness, gender equality, bullying, well-being, and include dedicated questions on CSE. 
As one of the key partners in the National Curriculum reform, UNFPA is building the capacities of curriculum authors to evaluate the existing curriculum and develop a new one. International standards and assessment tools in CSE will guide this process, ensuring the integration of CSE and life-skills topics into the new mandatory national curriculum. 

UNFPA will also support MER in organizing Education Week in May 2025, contributing to organization of a national conference with local and regional education experts and organizing a side event on Dual Education in the Vocational Education and Training (VET) system. 
Building on 2024 achievements, UNFPA will pilot a curriculum-based school club on health education, providing training and continuous support to 30 teachers from various schools. 

In 2026, UNFPA will continue to support the integration of health education, including comprehensive sexuality education (CSE), into the formal curriculum as part of the national curriculum reform. The working group responsible for the subject Me and Society will receive technical support to integrate these topics while developing the key curricular products, including the conceptual framework, the curriculum, and the methodological guide for teachers. Once these materials are finalized, UNFPA will begin delivering a long-term in-service capacity-building programme for the first cohort of Me and Society teachers who will start implementing the curriculum in September 2027.

Additionally, UNFPA will continue to provide technical support to MER in the process of institutionalizing the menstrual health and hygiene programme. As part of this process, UNFPA will conduct an assessment of the use of public funds by schools during the 2026–2027 school year and the actual access of girls to menstrual pads. The findings will inform the design of the fund disbursement process for the resources already allocated by MER for the 2027–2028 school year.

Building on the experience of previous years in supporting parents of adolescents to strengthen their knowledge of health and sexuality education topics—enabling them to better support the healthy development of their children—and in line with MER’s initiative to develop an ecosystem of parenting programmes, UNFPA will provide technical support for the development of a legal framework on parenting and will pilot a parenting programme.

Following the School Barometer research conducted last year, UNFPA will support a communication campaign to disseminate the findings. The organization will also support the National Pupils’ Council to share the results with their peers, consult them on recommendations and solutions, and present these during Education Week.

Finally, UNFPA will contribute to the collection of data on health behaviours among school-aged children through the HBSC study, in order to inform evidence-based decision-making in the education and health sectors.

projects.name: Ensuring the interlinkages between violence against women and violence against children are comprehensively researched and evidence-based recommendations are developed
projects.description:
UNFPA and UNICEF will conduct a systematic review to explore interventions that simultaneously prevent or respond to violence against women (VAW) and violence against children (VAC), aiming to identify common components and mechanisms that contribute to the reduction of intimate partner violence (IPV) and VAC. This research will enhance the understanding of key contextual drivers—psychological, social, and structural—that fuel prevalent forms of violence against girls, boys, and women, including shared drivers across multiple forms of violence. The findings will also shed light on effective interventions that can reduce both violence against children and women.

Building on these insights, UNICEF and UNFPA will support national research to document successful interventions addressing both forms of violence, particularly those targeting the transformation of harmful social and gender norms that perpetuate such violence. The research will explore the implications of its findings, examining how these insights can contribute to advancing the field and improving outcomes for both women and children.

In addition, UNFPA and UNICEF will jointly review various parenting and caregiver interventions aimed at supporting caregivers in two key areas: (i) equipping them with the skills to provide nurturing care and (ii) strengthening their mental health and emotional well-being. Given that children’s gender identity begins to develop in early childhood, and that gender-unequal norms can limit their life trajectories, the interventions will focus on incorporating positive gender socialization and promoting gender equality from the outset.

UNFPA will provide comprehensive support to the Government of the Republic of Moldova through targeted initiatives aimed at strengthening services for perpetrators of gender-based violence (GBV). UNFPA will also support the development of a national concept for services targeting GBV perpetrators, including the revision and enhancement of existing national standards to ensure alignment with international best practices.

In collaboration with key government agencies, such as the probation, penitentiary, and police departments, UNFPA will assist in designing and adapting domestic violence rehabilitation programs. These programs will incorporate both early prevention measures and targeted interventions aimed at reducing recidivism and promoting behavioral change among perpetrators.

To ensure continuous improvement and accountability, UNFPA will develop a comprehensive evaluation framework to assess the effectiveness and impact of perpetrator rehabilitation programs. Furthermore, a high-level advocacy event will be organized to promote the implementation of Article 16 of the Istanbul Convention, emphasizing the importance of addressing and rehabilitating perpetrators as a critical component of preventing future violence.

Through these initiatives, UNFPA aims to enhance the national response to GBV, fostering a more comprehensive and effective approach to addressing the root causes of violence in Moldova.

projects.name: Digital Literacy Assessment of Adult Population in Moldova
projects.description:
The ITU-ILO project “Inclusive and productive employment in Moldova”, will be assessing the digital literacy of the adult population, targeting adults aged 45+ in rural areas, and focusing on women and disadvantaged groups. The project will aim to assess digital literacy levels among adults, identifying skill gaps that affect employment, with the goal to improve employability by addressing these gaps and providing insights into necessary technological skills.

In alignment with national policy documents, such as ‘Moldova Europeană 2030’ and the ‘Educația 2030’ program, there is a strong emphasis on developing an accessible, flexible, and relevant system for continuous adult education. This focus includes enhancing digital competencies and leveraging information technologies to improve digital literacy across various adult groups. In response to a request from the Ministry of Education and Research in 2021, the ILO is supporting the promotion of digital literacy for adults (45-65) in rural areas, with a particular focus on low-skilled / low-educated populations, women and disadvantaged groups.

The project proposes a comprehensive assessment of digital literacy among the above-mentioned segments of the adult population in Moldova. The assessment will focus on digital skills, evaluating current competencies and identifying technological skill gaps that impact employment and employability of low-skilled and disadvantaged adults. The primary objective is to gauge digital skills in rural areas, identify gaps, and provide insights into technological skills necessary for improving employability for unemployed and disadvantaged populations.

The ITU will be responsible for designing the methodology for the assessment, conducting the assessment, and drafting a report, including recommendations. The assessment will serve as a catalyst for creating and implementing training programs that address skills needed for everyday activities, using digital government services, and improving employability, with a particular focus on gender-related needs and challenges.

projects.name: Strengthened gender data systems for sustainable development in ECA region
projects.description:
The planned activities are implemented jointly with  NBS, and are part of the implementation of the national statistical household survey “Gender-Based Violence Against Women and Other Forms of Interpersonal Violence.” This survey represents a critical step toward strengthening evidence-based policymaking and monitoring in the area of gender equality and human rights. Key preparatory phases include the design and testing of the survey methodology and data collection instruments, culminating in a pilot survey to be conducted by the end of 2025. These preparatory steps are essential to ensure the reliability, validity, and cultural relevance of the final tools used in full-scale data collection. The survey is implemented by the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS), in accordance with the Eurostat EU-GBV methodology and aligned with other relevant international statistical and human rights standards. Full-scale data collection is scheduled for 2026, following the completion and refinement of tools and methodology based on the pilot survey results.

Importantly, the implementation of the GBV Survey is a national commitment included in the National Action Plan for the Accession of the Republic of Moldova to the European Union for 2025–2028 (NAP EU-RM), under Chapter 18 – Statistics. This reinforces Moldova’s alignment with EU integration objectives and the strengthening of national statistical capacity.

This activity is also an integral part of the Action Plan under the National Programme on Preventing and Combating Violence Against Women for 2023–2027, reinforcing its relevance at the national policy level. By contributing directly to the implementation of this programme, the activity supports Moldova’s broader commitments to preventing and addressing violence against women and ensuring coordinated, multisectoral responses in line with national priorities and international human rights obligations.  

At the same time, the survey is critical for generating updated data for Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) indicators 5.2.1 and 5.2.2, which monitor the proportion of women and girls aged 15 and older who have experienced physical, sexual, or psychological violence in the previous 12 months. Gender-based violence (GBV) remains one of the most pervasive and entrenched forms of gender inequality. Reliable data on its prevalence is essential for tracking progress in the prevention and response to GBV, as well as for advancing gender equality and the empowerment of women and girls in Moldova.

projects.name: Support to the Government of the Republic of Moldova is provided in its formulation and effective implementation of the national industrial development programme and policy through institutional capacity-building
projects.description:
Over recent years, the Government of the Republic of Moldova has undertaken measures to improve the overall competitiveness of the economy by increasing industrial productivity, stimulating entrepreneurship and encouraging knowledge and innovation transfer through capacity development and the adoption of international standards and best practices, with the overarching objective of full integration into European Union markets and global value chains. In June 2022, the Republic of Moldova received European Union candidate status, marking a significant milestone towards strengthened integration with European Union markets and processes. This strategic direction is further reinforced in the National Development Strategy “European Moldova 2030”, endorsed in November 2022.

In light of current multifaceted challenges, including those related to energy, food, value and supply chains that are causing notable economic distress, particularly in the areas of energy security, regional logistics and economic competitiveness, there is a pressing need for a comprehensive industrial policy to accelerate digitalisation and the greening of the industrial sector. There is also a need for a structured capacity-building programme to address constraints and barriers to effective industrial policymaking.

These objectives will be addressed by capitalising on UNIDO’s experience and expertise in conducting diagnostic research, delivering capacity development activities and providing strategic normative policy advice and process facilitation. This will also facilitate the formulation of the UNIDO Programme for Country Partnership (PCP) with the Republic of Moldova.

projects.name: Trade Facilitation Strengthened via Modernized National Transit System of the Customs Service
projects.description:
Project Title: Development and Implementation of the National Transit System (NTS) of the Customs Service of the Republic of Moldova, compatible with NCTS Phase 5 (NTS-NCTS)
The overall objective of this project is to increase the CSRM trade facilitation and operational capacity, in the context of implementation of the EU - Moldova Association Agreement and the Strategic Framework for EU-Republic of Moldova Customs Cooperation, through the development and implementation of NTS-NTCS to prepare for Moldova's accession to the Common Transit Convention.
The specific objectives of the project are the following: 
•	To develop a National Transit System (NTS-NCTS) based on Web technologies aligned with the NCTS-P5 (if circumstances allow NCTS-P6) specifications and national requirements, including country specific deviations and the link with the Centrally operated/IE Convertor Application (connectivity with countries using NCTS phase 4). The NTS-NCTS will be developed using “open source" technologies, so that its functionality is not conditioned by any licenses. The NCTS-P5 module should be developed so that it could be used separately from ASYCUDAWorld, therefore it should not be developed on the ASYCUDAWorld development framework (middleware); 
•	To implement the NTS-NCTS capabilities into the operational CSRM ASYCUDA environment, ensuring full interoperability with existing and prospective ASYCUDAWorld system;  
•	To train the end-users of the system, both Customs officers and trade community, accordingly;
•	To further strengthen the trade facilitation by simplifying the trading environment in terms of customs procedures and documentation, while improving the customs supervision and monitoring.

Effects, impact and results: 

The Customs Service of the Republic of Moldova (CSRM) has successfully met all key national milestones set for 2024:
•	The implementation of additional ASYCUDAWorld modules and functionalities has been successfully completed, ensuring the operational application of the new Customs Code of the Republic of Moldova as of 1 January 2024. These components have been gradually deployed from that date
•	The NTS-NCTS system was piloted starting 1 July 2024 for a three-month period, in accordance with the National Project Plan (NPP) established between CSRM and DG TAXUD
•	The nationwide rollout of the NTS-NCTS system was completed on 1 October 2024
•	Visibility and communication events were successfully organized

To facilitate ongoing collaboration between EUD, CSRM, and UNCTAD in preparing for CTC accession while ensuring uninterrupted support, a revised version of the DoA, including the updated Workplan, has been submitted to EUD. This amendment extends the project duration to 34 months at no additional cost, ensuring:
•	UNCTAD’s continued support for the availability and operational continuity of CSRM’s NTS-NCTS P5, considering that NTS will initially operate for national transit only, requiring further reconfiguration to enable common transit


•	Assistance to CSRM’s National Service Desk in resolving incidents and handling requests from NCTS NTA end-users (e.g., economic operators, customs officers, the National Project Manager, and the national application management team), ensuring smooth operations during the transition phase
•	Support for the reconfiguration of CSRM’s NTS-NCTS system to enable common transit upon the commencement of CTC operations
•	Technical assistance for a potential upgrade of the system to NCTS-P6, if conditions permit

projects.name: Enhanced Customs Digitalization for Trade Facilitation and EU Integration in Moldova
projects.description:
II.	Project Title: Digitalization of Customs Services in Moldova (PHASE 1 and 2)
In short: The project modernizes Moldova’s customs operations by introducing digital tools for e-commerce processing, electronic certificates of origin, and customs decision management. It improves efficiency, reduces paperwork, and enhances communication between customs and traders.
Start date: 30.06.2021 (beyond UNSDCF)

Review of expected accomplishments and activities:
These projects are governed by the Contribution Agreement signed between European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) and the United Nations Conference on Trade and Development (UNCTAD) with the purpose to:
•	Phase 1 
•	Support to the Customs Service in facilitating cross-border e-commerce through the digitisation of pre-arrival processing for postal and express consignments (E-Commerce Project)
•	Support to the Customs Service in implementing Electronic Certificates of preferential Origin (eCPO Project)
•	Phase 2 
•	Digitalising the Customs decision making and decision management processes by implementing the CSRM Customs Decisions Management System. The single repository of Customs decisions will be interfaced with the CSRM ASYCUDAWorld Customs Declaration Processing System to enable automatic verification checks i.e. check the existence and validity of individual customs decisions (Deliverable 1).
•	Simplifying the trading environment and enhance the transparency of customs clearance processes by implementing the CSRM Trader Dashboard (Deliverable 2).
•	Improving the overall efficiency and digitalisation of Customs operations, enabling a paperless environment (Deliverable 3).

Effects, impact and results: 
•	eCommerce  
•	Express shipments 
	Following the legislative changes effective 1st August 2024, there has been a significant rise in the volume of electronic Manifests and Airwaybills submitted by express couriers
	During the initial testing phase, only two participants were involved. However, the number of express operators utilizing the new system has steadily grown, increasing from 5 in August 2024 (when the legislation was implemented) to 12 by December 2024
	Although the number of express couriers using system-to-system information exchange increased from 5 to 12, the proportion of shipments eligible for maximum simplifications (Categories 1 & 2) remains unchanged at approximately 98%. This indicates that the vast majority of shipments can still be released immediately upon arrival, without requiring further formalities such as the submission of H6/H1 customs declarations
	The new system has had a more substantial impact on major express operators, given the high volume of transactions they process (e.g. operator with 534,065 transactions per month)
	There is still room for improvement. A review of the data is recommended to identify additional ways to optimize processes. For instance, some express couriers handle a higher volume of simplified declarations. This raises the question of whether a system-to-system exchange for H6-simplified declarations should be developed and integrated into the current version
•	Postal shipments 
	The volume of parcels processed through Posta Moldovei remains substantial
	A large majority of postal items arriving in Moldova are accompanied by information from the origin. In December 2024, 94.8% of postal items included electronic advance data (EAD), a figure comparable to the average of 95.57% observed across Europe (Western and Eastern Europe combined). This high percentage enables the reuse of existing information, eliminating the need for additional data capture.
	Despite this progress, Posta Moldovei continues to face challenges in transmitting the required information for imports (e.g. duplicates)
•	The eCommerce outputs from the EBRD funded project (post and express) have been officially communicated to the WTO Trade Facilitation Committee 
•	The eCommerce Postal solution implemented in Moldova has been presented during global WCO-UPU events in Brussels in November 2024. and at UNCTAD Global Supply Chain Forum, May 2024
•	Customs Decisions Management System (CDMS)
•	The Customs Decisions Management System (CDMS) was presented to and validated by DGTAXUD on 29 February 2024. As of end 2024, a total of 215 applications have been processed, resulting in 174 active authorizations
•	Trader Dashboard 
•	The Trader Portal and CDMS were developed on the same open-source platform as the NCTS-MD. Both solutions are seamlessly integrated within the same platform as NCTS and are fully interfaced with the NCTS, along with the CSRM ASYCUDAWorld system. Currently, there are 1,676 active users on the new integrated platform (Trader Dashboard – CDMS – NCTS)
•	Electronic Certificate of Origin
•	The electronic Certificate of Origin solution has been presented to the DG TAXUD together with a brief presentation of all deliverables under Phase I and II, receiving very good feedback
•	DG TAXUD indicated that the sub-component covering the EUR-1/EUR-MED certificates can be deployed in other contracting parties to the PEM convention taking into consideration the fact that o ASYCUDA user countries are party to the Convention (Western Balkans: Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Kosovo; Mediterranean countries: Palestine, Jordan, Lebanon, Syria; Eastern Partnership countries: Moldova and Georgia)
